subject: math
title: A-Math quadratics: completing the square, discriminant and inequalities

questions: Half of 6 is what, and what area is the missing corner?
How does the area picture show x^2 + 6x + 9 = (x+3)^2?
segments.say: Start with x^2 + 6x drawn as area: an x-by-x square with two strips. Half of 6 is 3, so each strip is 3-by-x. Slide one strip below the square and look at the gap: a 3-by-3 corner, area 9. Fill it in and the shape is one big square, (x + 3) by (x + 3): completing the square is literally completing a square.

questions: What are the three cases for the sign of D, and what does each say about the roots?
segments.say: Now the discriminant. For ax^2 + bx + c, D = b^2 - 4ac, and its sign is the whole story. Watch the parabola sink: above the axis D is negative and there are no real roots, touching gives D = 0 and one repeated root, crossing twice gives D positive and two real roots.

questions: Which values split the number line for x^2 - 4 > 0, and why?
What does the test at x = 0 tell you about the middle region?
segments.say: Turn to the inequality x^2 - 4 > 0. Roots first: x = -2 and x = 2 split the line into three regions. Travel with the probe and test: x = -3 passes, x = 0 fails, x = 3 passes. Only the outer regions work, so the solution is x < -2 or x > 2.

questions: For x^2 + 1 = 0, the discriminant is -4 - so what are the roots?
What one word in 'no real roots' does the trap ignore?
segments.say: Spring the trap on purpose with x^2 + 1 = 0, where D = -4. The curve never touches the real axis, so there are no real roots - but read the word real. The roots have left the real line: x = i and x = -i, two complex roots.

questions: How do you complete the square for x^2 + 6x?
What does the sign of the discriminant tell you?
segments.say: Now work through the worksheet in pairs, checking each answer against the completing the square and discriminant sections of your student notes. Last, the exit ticket - on your own, no talking - and remember: roots first, then test each region, and no real roots is not no solution.
segments.watchFor: A negative discriminant means the equation has no solution. Listen for students who read D < 0 as no answer at all. Send them back to the word real: No real roots is not no solution: the equation still has two complex roots.
